articles.headline: The Other Side (poem)
articles.author: Ellen W. Harper
articles.summary: The following poem was written by Mrs. Frances Ellen W. Harper, our talented countrywoman. THE OTHER SIDE. 'You've heard, no doubt, of Irish bulls, / And how they blunder thick and fast...' (A poem addressed to O'Reilly on Black soldiers' service and loyalty.)

articles.headline: Letter from a Philadelphia teacher at Snow Hill, Md.
articles.author: Martha P. Williams
articles.summary: Datelined Philadelphia, July 23d, 1867. The writer, a Philadelphia teacher, left Philadelphia on 1 Nov. last to open a freedmen's school in the South, settling at Snow Hill, southeastern Maryland, where she taught up to sixty-seven day and forty night scholars. Signed 'Martha P. Williams, of Philadelphia.' (MIGRATION: Philadelphia teacher gone South.)

articles.headline: Time to Dance (discourse at Cherry Street Baptist Church)
articles.summary: This was the subject of a very able discourse by Rev. T. R. Miller, pastor of the Cherry Street Baptist Church, on Sabbath evening, Oct. 20th. The church was well filled with an attentive audience; the discourse, drawn out by a written address to Mr. Miller from a member of his congregation, argued there is no warrant in Scripture to dance for pleasure.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Daniel McCollom)
articles.author: Daniel McCollom
articles.summary: Information wanted of his brother, James [surname unclear] of North Carolina, formerly of Washington, D.C. (seen 1863 at Newbern, N.C., in Government service); also of James Dement, left in Washington, D.C. Address Daniel McCollom, 255 Currant Alley, Phila. N.B. Ministers in Newbern and elsewhere requested to read the notice. Nov. 2-4t.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Thomas Lewis, formerly Thomas Jones, Norristown)
articles.author: Thomas Lewis
articles.summary: Information wanted of relatives, among them John Anderson, and Rachel and Isabella Anderson. Any information of their whereabouts thankfully received by Thomas Lewis (formerly Thomas Jones), Norristown, Pa. Nov. 9-4t.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On Tuesday, October 29th, at the residence of the bride's parents, by the Rev. J. B. Reeve, Mr. Richard Richardson, of Annapolis, Md., to Miss Elizabeth Adger, daughter of Robert Adger, of this city. No cards. (Other marriages this issue were out of town: Pittsburg, Pa., and four at Terre Haute, Ind.)
people: father of the bride, of this city (Philadelphia)

articles.headline: Furniture -- R. M. Adger's New & Second Hand Furniture Store (advertisement)
articles.summary: FURNITURE. R. M. ADGER'S New & Second Hand Furniture Store, No. 710 Lombard St., under Liberty Hall, where he has constantly on hand all kinds of articles for housekeepers. Date code 'oct3' -- new this quarter (after the Sept. 28 cutoff).
people: proprietor, furniture store, 710 Lombard St. under Liberty Hall

articles.headline: Dentists and Herb Doctors -- Dr. T. M. Kennard & Bro. (advertisement, two addresses)
articles.summary: DENTISTS AND HERB DOCTORS. Dr. T. M. Kennard & Bro. respectfully inform their friends and former patrons that they have opened their office at 832 Carpenter Street, AND 717 Lombard Street, where Dentistry in all its branches will be attended to. Dr. Kennard also studies botany and the medicinal qualities of herbs. Ad dated Feb. 7, 1866 (standing). This printing lists BOTH 832 Carpenter and 717 Lombard; the DB entry (Run #99) records only 832 Carpenter -- the 717 Lombard address may already be present or may be new.
people: proprietor, dentist/herb doctor, 832 Carpenter St. and 717 Lombard St.

articles.headline: Personal -- Rev. B. T. Tanner preached at Bethel and Union A.M.E., Philadelphia
articles.summary: PERSONAL. Rev. B. T. Tanner, of Frederick, Md., was in our city last Saturday and Sunday. At 3 o'clock on Sabbath he preached in Bethel church, from 1 Corinthians xvi. 13; at night he preached at the Union A. M. E. church, from Acts ix. 6. Our readers will remember that Brother Tanner is the author of the excellent work 'An Apology for African Methodism.'
people: preached at Bethel and Union A.M.E., Philadelphia (Rev., of Frederick, Md.)

articles.headline: Revival at the A.M.E. Zion church (Rev. John A. Williams)
articles.summary: REVIVAL. The protracted meeting at the A. M. E. Zion church, under the pastoral care of the Rev. John A. Williams, is still going on. We are informed that about fifty persons have professed a hope in Christ Jesus. (Philadelphia A.M.E. Zion = Big Wesley / First Colored Wesley, Lombard St. -- FLAGGED.)

articles.headline: Death of Richard P. Gibbs
articles.summary: DEATH OF RICHARD P. GIBBS. A few weeks ago Rev. Richard P. Gibbs, pastor of the A. M. E. Church at Savannah, Ga., left this city for his post, returning from a visit to his family and a business tour in the interest of his Church. Arriving at Savannah he was suddenly prostrated by severe illness, and on Thursday, November 7th, breathed his last. His funeral took place in this city; the services were held in Union Church, Coates street, and were conducted by the pastor, Rev. Wm. Moore. (Resolutions of the Preachers' Association appear on p.3 -- see event.)
people: deceased; late pastor A.M.E. Church, Savannah, Ga.; funeral held in Philadelphia (Rev.)
pastor, Union A.M.E. Church, Coates street; conducted the funeral (Rev.)

articles.headline: Before the Supreme Court -- the Miles railroad-car exclusion case
articles.summary: BEFORE THE SUPREME COURT. The case of Mrs. Miles before the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania, in an action against the Railroad Company to recover damages, she having been forcibly ejected from the cars of the Company by one of the conductors. The Court decided that the plaintiff was not entitled to recover, holding that the providing of separate cars for colored persons was following the established law of custom. The editor notes the decision refers only to the law as it stood before the Legislative enactment of last March, the case having occurred prior to, and not since. (STREET-CAR / railroad-car exclusion topic.)

articles.headline: An Apology for African Methodism -- book for sale at the A.M.E. Book Depository (advertisement)
articles.summary: AN APOLOGY FOR AFRICAN METHODISM. By Rev. B. T. Tanner. JUST ISSUED. An excellent work of 400 pages, can be had at the A. M. E. Book Depository, No. 631 Pine Street, for a small sum. (New ad this quarter; confirms the Book Depository address as 631 Pine Street.)

articles.headline: Personal -- clergy appointments (J. B. Hamilton to Savannah; Theo. Gould to Camden)
articles.summary: PERSONAL. Bishop Wayman has transferred Rev. J. B. Hamilton, of the Philadelphia Conference, to the Georgia Conference of the A. M. E. Church, and appointed him to the charge at Savannah, made vacant by the death of the Rev. Richard P. Gibbs. Rev. Theo. Gould, Agent of the Book Concern, has been appointed to the charge at Camden, N. J., vice J. B. Hamilton transferred. (MIGRATION: a Philadelphia-Conference minister sent South.)
people: transferred from the Philadelphia Conference to the Savannah charge (Rev.)
Agent of the Book Concern; appointed to the Camden, N.J. charge (Rev.)

articles.headline: Rev. Newman Hall at Bethel Church
articles.summary: REV. NEWMAN HALL AT BETHEL CHURCH. 'Let the brother of low degree rejoice that he is exalted,' James i. 9, was the text of a discourse delivered at Bethel Church last Sunday evening by Rev. Newman Hall, the popular English minister, whose lectures and sermons during the past few weeks have awakened so much interest in religious circles. He was listened to by a very large congregation with the most earnest attention.
people: English minister; delivered a discourse at Bethel Church, Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Camden, N.J. (Macedonia A.M.E.; Snow Hill corner-stone)
articles.author: J. B. Hamilton
articles.summary: A letter from Camden, N.J. On November 3d, by previous arrangement, Rev. Stephen Smith and Rev. Redman Fauset and the writer met at Snow Hill, N.J., to lay the corner-stone of the new A.M.E. Church; Rev. Redman Fauset preached from John i. 29 and Rev. Stephen Smith from Haggai i. 8; the collection was $151.56. On Wednesday evening, Oct. 23d, twelve of the writer's congregation surprised him at his boarding-place with a gift of $41.51; the committee were Mrs. M. F. Dill, Mrs. R. M. Barnes, Miss M. J. Polk, Mrs. M. Wellet, Mrs. M. Patterson, Mrs. E. A. Stidum. ('Macedonia still lives.') Signed J. B. Hamilton, Camden, N.J., Nov. 11, 1867.
people: preached at the Snow Hill corner-stone laying (Rev.)
preached at the Snow Hill corner-stone laying (Rev.)

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Married in Philadelphia, November 12th, by Rev. D. Dorrell, Mr. Rasmus G. Haskins, of Richmond, Va., to Miss Rebecca Washington, of Philadelphia, Pa. Married in Philadelphia, November 12th, by the same, Mr. David Brown, of Baltimore, to Miss Rosanna [surname uncertain], of Camden, N.J. At the residence of the bride, West Philadelphia, November 14th, 1867, by Rev. H. J. Rhodes, Mr. Robert Waters, of Maryland, to Mrs. Martha Ann Young, of Alexandria, Virginia. (Also, out of scope: a marriage at Xenia, Ohio, and one at Bridgeton, N.J.)
people: officiating minister, the two Philadelphia marriages of Nov. 12 (Rev.)
officiating minister, West Philadelphia marriage of Nov. 14 (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Campbell
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Rev. E. Weaver: Dear Doctor -- Bishop Campbell reports before leaving home to attend the Texas and Louisiana Conferences (Helena, Galveston, New Orleans). He received toward his travel expenses from Bethel Church, Philadelphia, Rev. D. Dorrell, pastor, $40.00; from Bethel Church, Trenton, N.J., Rev. J. M. Williams, pastor, $7.00; and from Rev. Joshua Woodson, pastor of Fleet Street Church, Brooklyn, N.Y., $15.00 for Missions in the Valley of the Mississippi. He left Philadelphia Thursday, October 3d, and traveled via Richmond, Ind., Belleville and Cairo, Ill., Paducah, Nashville, Helena and Vicksburg. Signed J. P. Campbell, Vicksburg, Miss., Nov. 12, 1867.
people: pastor of Bethel Church, Philadelphia (Rev.); gave $40 to Bishop Campbell
pastor of Bethel Church, Trenton, N.J. (Rev.); gave $7

articles.headline: Death of Our Oldest Itinerant
articles.summary: It becomes our duty to again announce the death of a beloved minister. A few weeks since we published the death of Rev. R. P. Gibbs, and to-day we chronicle the demise of Rev. Jeremiah [H./G.] Balaugh, on the 25th inst., in the 83d year of his age. In the early days of the Church Father Balaugh was an earnest advocate of the Gospel of Christ; he labored in the Baltimore and New York Conferences, in Canada, and lastly in the Philadelphia Annual Conference. A notice of the funeral exercises will appear in our next. (Surname/initial uncertain -- see flags; the Preachers' Association resolutions are on p.3.)

articles.headline: Personal -- visiting clergy (J. R. V. Thomas; A. L. Stanford)
articles.summary: Revs. J. R. V. Thomas, of the Virginia Conference, and A. L. Stanford, of the Baltimore Conference, paid our city a visit this week. (Also noted this week: editor Rev. Elisha Weaver absent collecting debts; Rev. James Lynch has written to the New Orleans Advocate; an article on 'Ministerial Education' by Wm. E. Matthews, Esq., is forthcoming.)
people: visited Philadelphia (Rev., of the Baltimore Conference)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting Notice (Peter Gardiner)
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: My third round of Quarterly Meetings: Nov. 30th the Quarterly Conference will meet at 2 o'clock, Saturday afternoon; December 7th, Quarterly Meeting will commence on Saturday evening; and also at Bordentown, with a General Class, on Friday evening, December 13th, 1867. Peter Gardiner.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (children of Malinda Smith; Millville, N.J.)
articles.summary: Information wanted of Melissa Walker, who belonged to Richard Christian and was sold to Dr. Boothe; also of Waverly Johnson, Alexander Johnson, William Woodson, Chloe Woodson, and Archie Woodson, sold to Richmond, Va. Any information of the above named children of Malinda Smith, formerly of Amelia County, Virginia, will be gratefully acknowledged by (the inquirer), care of Whitall Tatum [as printed], Millville, New Jersey. Nov. 10-3t.

events.name: Public meeting of the colored men of Gloucester County, N.J. (taxation without representation)
events.location: A.M.E. Church, Gloucester County, N.J. (West Jersey; Woodbury dateline)
events.description: Reported in a 'Letter from New Jersey' signed W.W.G. (Rev. Wm. W. Grimes), Woodbury, N.J. On 10 Oct. 1867 the colored people of Gloucester County held a public meeting in the A.M.E. Church. Called to order by Rev. Wm. W. Grimes; first organized electing Jeremiah Douglass president, E. Johnson and Henry Dickerson vice presidents, James Tudas and Joseph Clark secretaries. Grimes offered resolutions protesting taxation without representation and asserting the elective franchise. Rev. H. Dickerson favored them; Mr. Hunt (white) objected in part. After adoption the permanent organization was formed: Alfred Craig president; Jeremiah Douglas and Henry Dickerson vice presidents; James Tudas and Wm. W. Grimes secretaries; Benjamin Anderson treasurer; Grimes appointed to consult a lawyer. ('So we are not asleep in West Jersey.') Pastor J. S. Leakens and the Millville quarterly conference are mentioned; Rev. Benjamin Parker on the Gloucestown circuit noted. West Jersey (Philadelphia Conference) names kept in text only except the AME clergyman Grimes.
attendees: called meeting to order; permanent secretary; appointed to consult counsel (Rev.)

events.name: Union Thanksgiving meeting -- Philadelphia district (Bishop Wayman's plan)
events.description: SPECIAL NOTICE. Bishop A. W. Wayman's plan for holding union thanksgiving meetings on Thursday, Nov. 28th, 1867. 2d district: Philadelphia and vicinity will meet at Bethel church, Philadelphia, at 10 o'clock; sermon by Rev. James M. Williams, of Trenton, N.J. (Other districts: Baltimore -- Bethel, Baltimore, sermon Rev. D. W. Moore; New York -- Bridge Street church, Brooklyn; Washington -- Israel Church, D.C., Rev. J. A. Mackay; Norfolk/Portsmouth -- St. John's, Norfolk, Bishop Wayman.) Pastors asked to raise special collections for worn-out preachers. Signed A. W. Wayman, Nov. 9. (THANKSGIVING observance.)
attendees: to preach, Bethel church Philadelphia (Rev., of Trenton N.J.; Phila. Conference)

events.name: Fair of the ladies of Bethel church, at Liberty Hall (for Missionary purposes)
events.description: FAIR. The ladies of Bethel church, and others, intend holding a fair for Missionary purposes during the holidays, at Liberty Hall, Lombard Street, to commence December 24, 1867. Season tickets 25 cents, single tickets 10 cents, to be had of the committee and at the A.M.E. Book Concern. Committee as printed: Mrs. Sarah Wilkins, President, 601 Pine Street; Mrs. Margaret Allen, Vice President, 282 Quince Street; Mrs. Tamar Marin [surname uncertain, VERIFY], Treasurer, 621 Pine Street; Mrs. Ann Winn [surname uncertain, VERIFY], Secretary, rear of 637 Lombard Street; Mrs. Mary Campbell, Assistant Secretary, 910 Addison Street. Nov. 9-1mo.
attendees: president of the fair committee, 601 Pine Street (Mrs.)

events.name: Juvenile Exhibition at Liberty Hall
events.description: EXHIBITION. A Juvenile Exhibition was held at Liberty Hall on Thursday, the 7th inst. There was a pretty full house, and the exercises of the little folks were very interesting; refreshments of ice-cream and cakes were served. The children were under the guidance and care of Mrs. Johnson and Mrs. Evans. (Surname-only women not linked.)

events.name: Bishop Wayman's appointments -- Philadelphia (Union, Bethel, Wesley churches)
events.location: Union, Bethel and Wesley churches, Philadelphia
events.description: BISHOP WAYMAN'S APPOINTMENTS. Sunday, November 17th -- morning, Union church, Philadelphia; afternoon, Bethel church, Philadelphia; night, Wesley church, Philadelphia. Then the West Jersey circuit: Monday Nov. 18th Woodbury, N.J.; Tuesday Nov. 19th Vineland, N.J.; Wednesday Nov. 20th Gouldtown, N.J.; Thursday Nov. 21st Bridgeton, N.J.; Friday Nov. 22d Salem, N.J.; then Laurel and Georgetown, Del.; Salisbury, Md.; Norfolk and Portsmouth, Va.; Eastville and Pungoteague, Va.; Baltimore (Ebenezer, Waters', Bethel, Dec. 8); Hagerstown, Md.; Greencastle and Chambersburg, Pa.
attendees: bishop making the appointments; to visit the Philadelphia churches Nov. 17 (Bishop)

events.name: Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference -- resolutions on the death of Rev. Richard P. Gibbs
events.description: RESOLUTIONS. The Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference deeply deplores the death of Rev. Richard P. Gibbs, a presiding officer of the Georgia Annual Conference; resolves to sympathize with his family and that the resolutions be published in the Christian Recorder and a copy sent to the widow. Signed J. B. Hamilton, Chairman; Wm. W. Gaines [surname uncertain, VERIFY], Secretary. Phila., Pa., Nov. 12, 1867.
attendees: chairman, Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference

events.name: Corner-stone laying of the new A.M.E. Church at Snow Hill, N.J.
events.location: Snow Hill, N.J. (West Jersey; Philadelphia Conference)
events.description: Reported in a Letter from Camden, N.J. (J. B. Hamilton). On Nov. 3d, 1867, Rev. Stephen Smith, Rev. Redman Fauset and the writer met at Snow Hill, N.J., to lay the corner-stone of the new A.M.E. Church. Rev. Redman Fauset preached from John i. 29; Rev. Stephen Smith preached from Haggai i. 8; the morning and afternoon collection was $151.56; the corner-stone was laid according to the ritual.

events.name: Fair of the ladies of the Lombard Street Central Presbyterian Church
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, below Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: FAIR. The ladies of the Lombard Street Central Presbyterian Church will hold a Fair for the sale of useful and fancy articles, at the Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, below Pine, commencing Wednesday, Nov. 27, and to continue two weeks, for the benefit of the Church. The Fair will be open every afternoon and evening, and all Thanksgiving Day. Season tickets 25 cts., single admission 10 cts. Nov. 23-1t. (No individual committee names printed.)

events.name: Exhibition by the scholars of Bethel Sunday-school at Liberty Hall
events.description: The scholars of Bethel Sunday-school will give an exhibition at Liberty Hall, on Thursday evening, the 5th proximo (December 5, 1867). (Announced in the editor's column, p.2.)

events.name: Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference -- resolutions on the death of Rev. Jeremiah Balaugh
events.description: RESOLUTIONS. The Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference announces the death of its aged father in the gospel, Rev. Jeremiah [G./H.] Balaugh, and deeply deplores his loss; resolves that the Philadelphia Annual Conference has lost one of its most esteemed members, and sympathizes with his family. The Rev. Jeremiah Balaugh labored in the Baltimore and New York Conferences, in Canada, and lastly in the Philadelphia Annual Conference, where he finished his labors at the age of 83 years. Signed, as Committee: Rev. William Moore, Rev. D. Dorrell, Rev. Stephen Smith.
attendees: committee, Preachers' Association resolutions; pastor of Bethel Church, Philadelphia (Rev.)
